reason: scopeInputSchema requires setOn (isoDate) and the scope proposal uses that schema as-is (turn-contract.ts scopeProposal). Nothing tells the brain today's date: renderState in agent.ts:42-60 has no date, the prompt has none, and SCOPE_QUESTIONS has no setOn question. The model has to invent the set date, and the reviewOn>=setOn check depends on that invented value.

judgeClaim tests the research span with quoteInPage, which is true only for 'grounds'. A span under MIN_QUOTE_WORDS(4) returns 'too_short', so a short span the page does carry gets the reason 'not on the page as fetched', is treated as misquoted, and is judged with quotedSpan undefined. The note says 'the research's quoted span is not on the page', which is false. The verdict itself still rests on the verifier's own grounded quote.

proseBlocks merges any list block into the previous block of the same kind across a blank line. listKind discards the digits, so a second list starting again at '1.' straight after a blank line joins the first and is renumbered. This only happens when no paragraph sits between the two lists. The test gap is coverage only.

The switcher prints nav.subject.name and the other companies' names without data-record (shell.ts:141,144), and so does the nav aria-label (shell.ts:167). The conversation's origin text goes into the header's band-context

, which has no data-record. visibleText() therefore checks them. The effect is false hits or misses in the vocabulary guard; users are not affected.

The submit handler adds the 'turn user' bubble and clears the box before the POST. If the POST fails, the catch turns the waiting line into 'Ed could not answer this'. The unsent message stays shown as sent and the failure reads as Ed's. The text is still visible in the bubble, which limits the loss.

Intake now saves Ed's plan only as a draft and leaves config.domainPlan at the identity version. buildPathView still builds the setup plan from config.domainPlan. setupStep still renders a 'Start research' form, and the server now refuses that with 409 until the plan is confirmed. The draft awaiting confirmation is not shown on that page.

runRerunBatch sets the notes to 'sent' with batch_id, then runs recordInsightReview, createBatchRun and the rerun_batch update, all before the try block. If any of those throws, the catch that fails the batch and its notes never runs, and rerun-notes.ts has no recovery for 'sent' notes.

The move_enquiry and verify_claim tools start rerunTogether jobs that call the batch revision and scoring models with no provider permission check. Neither runTool nor batch-rerun.ts checks either. The web routes that rerun do check, through assertAllModelsPermitted.

The rerun verb calls startAnalysisRun and then recordAnalysisRerun, which closes the flag as soon as the run starts. If the run later fails the flag is gone from the header and cannot be chosen again. The module comment says closing on start is intended, but nothing reopens the flag on failure.

actionRevisions returns why: head.note and actor: head.created_by whatever the audience. Unlike insightRevisions, it never applies the client-reads-only-own-notes rule. revision-view.ts:60-61 renders that reason and author to a client.

The new /c/:slug/documents route lists every current source for the subject (strategy, company, external research pack) with name, kind and uploader, and has no audience filter. guardPage lets a client open it. The Evidence page, by contrast, hides company material from clients.

startWebServer's close() only closes the server and unregisters the briefing writer; it never calls drainRunEvents. Briefings still in flight when the web process stops are dropped, while the CLI and the worker do drain.

The deep path stores research_corpus but calls researchThenAnswer, which ignores the corpus. It always runs a web research run and then answers. A Deep question asked of 'Your documents' spends web research instead of staying within the company's documents.

For Ed's own standing chat, conversationBody renders a note in place of composerHtml, but THREAD_JS still runs form.querySelector('textarea') on a null form. That throws at the top of the IIFE, and the artefact panel code concatenated after it never runs.

The claim sets drawn_note='Ed is reading it' and only succeeds when drawn_note differs. Only the catch block or a success resets it. If the process dies mid-read, the row keeps the reading note and no later job can claim it, so the document stays unread for good.
